messages:
maya: Quick sync — planning a community webinar + refapp launch next Tue. Need a short launch post, a concise benchmark narrative for social, webinar ops, and inbound routing to Sales. Agenda: 1) webinar outline 2) launch post draft 3) benchmark snapshot 4) lead routing. Who owns what? :calendar:
jordan: I can own the refapp demo + repo readiness. Plan: 30m hands-on lab (live demo) + 10m Q&A. Will push a demo video and a minimal 'get started' README by EOD Fri. Repo stub: https://github.com/redwood/refapp-onboarding (placeholder)
sam: I'll draft the launch post and a short tutorial (5-7 steps). For the benchmark narrative I want a 1-paragraph summary + a 3-line social blurb. Can someone paste the benchmark numbers or point me to the CSV?
ops: Eng-ML will drop numbers. Pinging @igor for the measured numbers. Also tracking params: please use utm_source=community&utm_campaign=onboard_refapp&utm_medium=social for all links.
registrations-bot: New regs so far: 12. Form: https://redwood.ai/webinar-register?utm=onboard_refapp — attendees list will be exported to SFDC campaign after the event.
igor: Quick measured outputs we ran yesterday: Llama2-13B-4bit on p4d, median per-token decode latency ~45ms at batch=8; cost estimate after batching + kernel opt ~ $0.003 / token. With KV prefix caching for typical 64-token prompts overall token spend dropped ~22% in our test rig. TL;DR: batching + caching -> ~2-3x cost improvement vs naive single-request serving. I'll drop raw CSV into #eng-ml.
maya: Perfect. Sam — please distill that into a conservative 3-line benchmark blurb + a 1-paragraph explainer for the blog. Suggested copy snippet to start from: 'By enabling batching and prefix caching, the reference app cut per-token spend by ~2.2x and reduced p95 latency by ~28%, making interactive LLM features affordable on modest infra.' Keep claims conservative and cite test setup.
sam: Drafting now. Blog blurb draft: 'In our reference app, batching and KV prefix caching reduced per-token costs by ~2.2x and trimmed p95 latency by ~28%. That makes interactive, near-real-time LLM features 2-3x cheaper to operate compared to naive serving setups.' I'll post the full draft in #marketing for feedback before Mon.
anya: Inbound routing plan: attendees who show up + fork/clone the refapp get routed as hot leads to AE queue 'community-inbound' in SFDC (campaign: W-ONBOARDREFAPP). Web registrants who don't attend go to Mailchimp nurture list 'community-onboard-30d'. Add a hidden field on the reg form: refapp=true so we can segment easily.
jeff: I'll own webinar ops (slides + runbook + speaker checklist). Need speaker list + slide deck draft by Mon EOD. Also proposing a promo: 20% Dedicated trial credit for attendees redeemable via promo code. Thoughts on gating?
maya: Love the promo — great incentive. Jordan, can you add a small "Run locally" section + a one-click Docker quickstart to the README before Fri so we can include a 'Try it now' CTA in the post?
jordan: On it. I'll add `./run-local.sh` and a Docker compose example. Quick snippet I'll include:
```bash
# run-local.sh (WIP)
docker-compose up --build -d
./scripts/populate-sample-data.sh
./run-local.sh --port 8080
```
maya: Timeline check — Fri EOD: repo + demo video; Mon: marketing draft + slides; Tue: webinar; Wed: publish blog + launch post + social push. Are we good with that cadence? :thumbsup:
sam: Good for me — I'll queue the social drafts and a short thread for X and LinkedIn. Will include a CTA to the repo and the webinar recording.
jordan: Demo video will be ~6 mins focused on 'how to integrate batching + KV cache' and one short segment on running locally.
igor: I'll also prepare a short 'benchmark appendix' that lists exact config (model, sequence lengths, batch sizes, HW) so we can attach it to the blog as technical notes.
maya: Great. I'll consolidate action items and send a short runbook after this thread. Thanks everyone — let's reconvene Tues pre-show 30 min before start.
registrations-bot: Reminder: form export scheduled Tue 23:30 UTC to SFDC export queue.
